subject: Clinica retention bifurcation & SIG evidence request
messages:
From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@clinica-health.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@clinica-health.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: retention granularity + SIG evidence for legal hold

Hi Rishi,

Quick note from our side — our legal team has a pending litigation hold that may require us to retain certain inference traces and access logs for a covered subset of tenant activity for up to 180 days. Before we proceed, we need to understand the feasible operational options and supporting evidence for SIG/CAIQ reviewers.

Specifically:
- Can Redwood support a customer-scoped exception (tenant-scoped) that retains access/auth logs for 180 days while keeping inference traces (model_inputs/model_outputs) at the standard 30-day TTL?
- If so, what is the minimal set of artifacts you can provide for SIG/CAIQ (e.g., process diagrams, retention matrix, proof-of-delete playbook, sampling evidence)?
- Can we request encrypted-at-rest keys be customer-managed for that tenant?

I've attached our SIG spreadsheet with the sections legal flagged (Clinica_SIG_Security_Questions.xlsx). Can you let me know what you need from our side and an estimated turnaround?

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lee
Head of IT Compliance, Clinica Health
marcus.lee@clinica-health.com

Attachment: Clinica_SIG_Security_Questions.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 120KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@clinica-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: retention granularity + SIG evidence for legal hold

Hi Marcus — thanks for the note and for sending the SIG sheet. Looping in Marissa (Customer Success) and Neha (Security) so we can scope the ask end-to-end.

High-level answers up front:
- Yes, we can support tenant-scoped retention exceptions for selected log classes. We typically treat access/auth logs (API auth, token issuance, IP/logging metadata) separately from model I/O traces.
- We can produce a retention matrix and a sampling-based proof-of-delete bundle for deleted inference traces. For access logs used for legal hold, we can extend retention to 180 days for that tenant and provide an audit manifest.
- Customer-managed encryption keys (CMK) are supported on our Private deployment; for Hosted customers we offer KMS integrations but not full bring-your-own-HSM in the standard plan — we'll need to check your deployment mode.

Preliminary proposed approach (to align on):
1) Bifurcated retention: access/auth logs = 180 days (tenant-scoped exception); inference traces = 30 days (default), with on-request export/redaction options.
2) Evidence pack: retention_matrix_v3.pdf (attached) + sample deletion manifest + CAIQ/SIG pointers + control ownership diagram.
3) Timeline: we can produce the evidence pack in ~5 business days once we confirm which log classes you need retained and the tenant IDs. For a formal change to retention we will require a signed addendum (DocuSign) that notes the exception window and SLA implications.

Action items:
- Marcus: confirm tenant IDs and whether Clinica prefers 90d/180d split for inference vs access logs (you mentioned 180d for everything — want to make sure).
- Marissa: can you confirm operational feasibility and whether we need a temporary hold while we produce the evidence?
- Neha: please advise on the SIG/CAIQ artifacts we should pull and any redaction constraints.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Attachment: retention_matrix_v3.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@clinica-health.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: retention granularity + SIG evidence for legal hold

Rishi / Marcus — we can implement a tenant-scoped retention exception. One quick operational note: enabling 180d retention for access logs will increase storage retention charges and will change how forensics exports are produced (we will need a short runbook for ad-hoc collections).

From an execution perspective: we can enable a temporary hold (no config change) for up to 7 days while security and legal review the evidence pack, or we can put the tenant on the longer retention policy once we have a signed addendum.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

—
Marissa Cole
Redwood Inference
Attachment: (none)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@clinica-health.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: retention granularity + SIG evidence for legal hold

Marcus — thanks for the clear ask. A few security considerations and what we can provide: 

What we can deliver (standard):
- Completed CAIQ sections relevant to data retention and secure disposal.
- SIG response bundle containing control narratives, diagrams, and sampled artifacts (we'll attach sig_response_bundle.zip).
- Retention matrix mapping (retention_matrix_v3.pdf) showing log classes, owners, and retention windows.
- Proof-of-delete sampling playbook (we produce deletion manifests + sample binary hashes for deleted objects).

Questions / constraints:
- Redaction vs retention: If Clinica accepts redaction of PII from inference traces (we can redact model inputs/outputs by token-level suppression and still keep metadata), that reduces the legal risk and storage footprint. Redaction is irreversible; legal sign-off required.
- CMK: Hosted customers can use cloud KMS integrations; if you need HSM-level isolation we should discuss a Private deployment (adds lead time).
- E-discovery timeline: for a compliant forensics export we need ~48–72 hours to assemble a manifest and sampling evidence once a formal request is filed.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus confirms whether redaction is an acceptable mitigation for inference traces.
2) If not, confirm tenant IDs and final retention windows per log class.
3) We produce SIG/CAIQ artifacts and a sample delete manifest within 5 business days.

Attachment: sig_response_bundle.zip (ZIP, 2.1MB)

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@clinica-health.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, legal@clinica-health.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: retention granularity + SIG evidence for legal hold

Rishi / Neha / Marissa — thanks. Clinica's legal team reviewed the options and will accept a mixed approach:
- Access/auth logs (API, token issuance, admin audit) -> 180 days (tenant-scoped exception).
- Inference traces (model inputs/outputs) -> retain 90 days (not 30) with strict role-based access and export auditing. Redaction is not preferred at this time.

We can sign the addendum with those windows. Please send the DocuSign link for the retention addendum and the SIG bundle once ready.
